title: Sessionize events in SQL
summary: Split each user's event stream into sessions after 30 minutes of inactivity.
prompt: Product analytics wants sessions. A user's session ends when **more than 30 minutes** pass without an event
from that user; an event exactly 30:00 after the previous one continues the session.
Return `user_id`, `session_start`, `session_end` (the first and last event's `at`) and `events`
`CAST(strftime('%s', at) AS INTEGER)` turns it into seconds, which avoids rounding trouble.
Gaps are per user: another user's events must never join or split your sessions.
setup: CREATE TABLE events (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, user_id INTEGER NOT NULL, at TEXT NOT NULL);
solution: SELECT user_id, at, CAST(strftime('%s', at) AS INTEGER) AS t FROM events
CASE WHEN t - LAG(t) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY t) <= 1800 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS is_new
SUM(is_new) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY t ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS session_no
SELECT user_id, MIN(at) AS session_start, MAX(at) AS session_end, COUNT(*) AS events
wrong: SELECT user_id, at, CAST(strftime('%s', at) AS INTEGER) AS t FROM events
CASE WHEN t - LAG(t) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY t) < 1800 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS is_new
SELECT user_id, at, SUM(is_new) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY t ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS session_no FROM marked
SELECT user_id, MIN(at) AS session_start, MAX(at) AS session_end, COUNT(*) AS events
FROM numbered GROUP BY user_id, session_no ORDER BY user_id, session_start;
SELECT user_id, at, CAST(strftime('%s', at) AS INTEGER) AS t FROM events
CASE WHEN t - LAG(t) OVER (ORDER BY t) <= 1800 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS is_new
SELECT user_id, at, SUM(is_new) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY t ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS session_no FROM marked
SELECT user_id, MIN(at) AS session_start, MAX(at) AS session_end, COUNT(*) AS events
FROM numbered GROUP BY user_id, session_no ORDER BY user_id, session_start;
MIN(at) AS session_start, MAX(at) AS session_end, COUNT(*) AS events
GROUP BY user_id, CAST(strftime('%s', at) AS INTEGER) / 1800
hints: Work in three steps: flag each event that starts a session, number the sessions with a running sum of the flags, then group.
An event starts a session when it is the user's first (`LAG` is NULL) or `t - LAG(t) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY t)` is over 1800.
`SUM(is_new) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY t ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING)` gives every event its session number; `GROUP BY user_id, session_no`.
